content.value: You can spend your Downtime crafting a new System or Module for your Mech. To craft an item you must have access to a Crafting Bay of equal or higher Tech Level to the item being crafted. You must also spend an amount of Scrap equal to the item's Salvage Value. The Scrap used must be of equal or higher Tech Level to the item being crafted.

During Downtime your Mech's SP and EP are fully restored and its Heat is reduced to 0 if your Union Crawler has a Mech Bay of the same or higher Tech Level as your Mech Chassis. Any Damaged Systems and Modules are restored to the Intact condition for free.
A Destroyed System or Module can be repaired to the Intact condition by spending an amount of Scrap equal to its Salvage Value. The Scrap must be of equal or higher Tech Level to the item.

You can trade Systems, Modules, and Scrap with other Pilots or with merchants at a Trading Bay. You can also buy and sell items. The price of items is typically equal to their Salvage Value in Scrap of the appropriate Tech Level.

You can spend your Downtime going on a Salvage Run to scavenge for parts and materials. The Mediator will determine what you find based on the surrounding environment and any narrative factors. Salvage Runs can be a source of adventure and danger.
You can spend your Downtime training to gain new Abilities. You gain 1 Training Point per week of Downtime which can be spent to learn new Abilities from your Class's Ability Trees.
Core Abilities cost 1 Training Point. Advanced and Hybrid Abilities cost 2 Training Points. Legendary Abilities cost 3 Training Points.

You can spend your Downtime exploring the surrounding area. This can lead to discovering new locations, meeting new NPCs, finding hidden caches of supplies, or uncovering information about the world. The Mediator will determine what you find based on the surrounding environment and narrative.
